explanation: I searched Mathlib for `primaryComponent` and `integerPrime`. The only declarations are `Ideal.primaryComponent` and `Ideal.primaryComponent_mem` in Algebra/Module/Torsion/PrimaryComponent.lean, plus `AddCommGroup.primaryComponent` and `mem_primaryComponent` in GroupTheory/Torsion.lean. Mathlib has no lemma linking the ideal-theoretic primary component (for the height-one prime `(p)` of ℤ) to the group-theoretic p-primary component. The library's own proof needs `Ideal.primaryComponent_mem`, `mem_primaryComponent`, `Ideal.span_singleton_pow` and `Submodule.mem_torsionBySet_iff`. Beyond those it needs a manual argument in both directions, with membership in a principal ideal and ℕ-versus-ℤ scalar conversion. That is more than one or two lines from a single declaration.
